paper_metadata.title: Electric Power Demand Portfolio Optimization by Fermionic QAOA with Self-Consistent Local Field Modulation

summary: The paper proposes FQAOA‑SCLFM, a fermionic QAOA variant with a Hartree–Fock driver incorporating self‑consistent local field modulation for a 20‑participant electricity demand portfolio problem. In noiseless simulations (p=10), the method achieves expected cost ratios ΔE_T/W_T as low as 0.007 for difficult periods (T=18,21), outperforming XY‑QAOA (~0.052–0.056) and prior FQAOA (~0.030) on the same instances. Experiments were conducted using a 20‑qubit statevector simulation in Qulacs.

experiments.description: Noiseless simulation study of FQAOA-SCLFM for electric power demand portfolio optimization across multiple time periods and QAOA depths, compared against XY-QAOA and prior FQAOA.

algorithm.variant: Fermionic QAOA with self-consistent local field modulation (FQAOA-SCLFM)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: classical parameter optimization to minimize expected cost; HF self-consistency iterated until convergence

hyperparameters.thop: set so first term of driver Hamiltonian cost range matches first term of cost Hamiltonian under constraints
hyperparameters.NT: number of reference points in time period T
hyperparameters.boundary_condition: periodic for odd number of fermions, anti-periodic for even number of fermions

algorithm.parameter_initialization: QAOA parameters optimized classically; HF iteration initialized with uniform fermion distribution n_l,0^HF = 1/MT

problem_formulation.encoding_details: one binary variable x_l per DR participant; computational basis state corresponds to bit string x in {0,1}^L
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize E_{T,x} = (1/NT) sum_{t in T} [ sum_{l,l'} sigma_{t,l,l'} x_l x_l' + (sum_l E[p_{t,l}] x_l - P'_{t,proc})^2 ] subject to sum_l x_l = M_T
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: hard constraint sum_l x_l = M_T enforced by constant-particle-number subspace; inequality procurement constraint absorbed into quadratic penalty term with P'_{t,proc}=P_{t,proc}+delta/2
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_p,T = sum_{l,l'} sigma_{T,l,l'} n_l n_l' + (1/NT) sum_{t in T} (P_t - P'_{t,proc})^2

problem_instance.description: Electric power demand portfolio optimization / negawatt trading using residential electricity usage data
problem_instance.dataset_name: Residential electricity usage database from Niigata University / Ref. [23]

dataset_specification.description: 20 residences, September 1-15, 2003; time periods T = 3i for i=0..7 with three reference times each

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: electricity usage of 20 residences used as negawatt supply; water-heater usage ignored; expected negawatt E[p_{t,l}] and covariance sigma_{t,l,l'} estimated from historical data following Ref. [8]
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: noiseless simulation; compare FQAOA-SCLFM against XY-QAOA and prior FQAOA at p=0,1,10; evaluate total negawatt, variance, and expected cost across all time periods

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: estimate sigma_{t,l,l'} and E[p_{t,l}] from historical residential electricity data; set P'_{t,proc}=1.5 kWh and M_T=5 for initial tests
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: compute total negawatt Pt,tot, variance sigma^2_{t,tot}, and expected cost Delta E_T from optimized probability distribution

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: HF energy decreases with iterations; QAOA cost improves with p

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or wall-clock speedup analysis is provided. The paper reports only empirical performance comparisons in expected cost and total negawatt stability.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: not analyzed; study limited to 20‑variable simulated QAOA circuits
limiting_factors: evaluation performed only in noiseless statevector simulation
problem size limited to 20 binary variables (20 qubits)
comparison only between quantum heuristic variants (XY‑QAOA, FQAOA, FQAOA‑SCLFM)
no comparison with classical optimization solvers for the portfolio problem
no asymptotic complexity or runtime scaling analysis

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper states numerical simulations were performed using the fast quantum simulator qulacs and reports no real QPU.
20 qubits inferred from 20 DR participants / binary variables x_l, one qubit per participant in basis encoding.
Circuit depth reported only as QAOA level p with experiments at p=0,1,10; no transpiled depth given.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided; only empirical performance comparisons versus XY-QAOA and prior FQAOA.
The paper claims improved performance of FQAOA‑SCLFM relative to XY‑QAOA and earlier FQAOA but does not compare against classical optimization methods or claim quantum advantage.
All results are noiseless simulations on 20‑variable instances.
